_comment: Template for an exploration's workflow DAG. Copy to project_workflow/<exploration>/workflow_dag.json and fill in. One object per computation node; edges are given by prev/next lists of node IDs. Each node has a UNIQUE integer `id` (identity, referenced by prev/next) and an integer `level` (tree depth: nodes that can run in parallel share a level; level = max(parent levels)+1). The scheduler sweeps by level and a node is ready when every prev is 'completed'. A node marked 'terminated' has been judged invalid and is OUT of the live graph: it never becomes 'completed', so nothing downstream of it can ever become ready. Keys beginning with '_' are documentation only -- do NOT copy them into a real workflow_dag.json (use scripts/new_dag.py, which strips them).

_node_format.name: human-readable node id, matches the run dir name where applicable
_node_format.description: short (<= ~120 chars) summary of what this node computes
_node_format.status: one of status_legend (start as 'pending', or 'blocked' with blocked_on)
_node_format.id: UNIQUE integer identity; the value referenced by other nodes' prev/next
_node_format.level: integer tree depth; parallel nodes share a level; level = max(parent levels)+1 (root=0)
_node_format.tool: computational software this node runs (vasp | phonopy | shengbte | ...), lowercase, matching its skill/reference name in reference/quick-ref.md; '' for a node that runs no batch job. This is what selects the health probe: .claude/skills/<tool>/scripts/probe.sh if it exists, else scripts/probe_generic.sh
_node_format.cluster: HPC cluster this node runs on (lonestar6 | frontera | local | ...)
_node_format.partition: SLURM partition / queue this job runs in (normal | development | gpu-a100 | ...); '' for local steps
_node_format.num_nodes: number of compute nodes requested (SLURM -N), as a string e.g. '4'; '' for local steps
_node_format.expected_start: expected/scheduled job start time (e.g. '2026-07-04 09:00' or queue ETA); '' if unknown
_node_format.request_time: requested walltime (HH:MM:SS). For a cluster node this is the SLURM -t. For a `cluster: local` node it is OPTIONAL and means the wall-clock cap the local-node runner enforces; leave '' to take that runner's 10-minute default
_node_format.job_id: slurm job id once submitted; '' until submitted
_node_format.elapsed_time: live wall-clock elapsed since the job started (HH:MM:SS, updated while status=running); '' if not started
_node_format.running_time: final total runtime once the job has finished (HH:MM:SS); '' until run
_node_format.blocked_on: OPTIONAL: what must be provided before this node can run; present only while status = 'blocked'
_node_format.terminated_reason: OPTIONAL: short (<= ~120 chars) reason this node was judged invalid; present only while status = 'terminated'
next: list of downstream node ids; [] if terminal
